mainTopic: Can a woman consecrate (הקדש) her future handiwork (מעשה ידיה), which right now belongs to her husband? The גמרא tests this with a chain of comparisons to a field that will only come back to its owner later.
overview: Earlier on the daf the גמרא discussed a woman who consecrates her handiwork. Right now that handiwork goes to her husband, so the consecration could only take effect later, once she is divorced. רבי אילא supports this with a seller who consecrates a field he is selling, effective when he buys it back. Then a chain of אמוראים each say 'מי דמי', meaning the comparison doesn't fit. רבי ירמיה says a field already sold is the better match, and that points against the woman. רב פפא says a pledged field matches better, and רב שישא בריה דרב אידי refines it to a field pledged for ten years. Both of those point in her favor. Finally רב אשי rejects even the ten-year field, because it has a fixed end date and a woman has none.

steps.title: רבי אילא compares the woman to a field being sold
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילא supports the idea that a woman can consecrate her future handiwork. He points to someone who consecrates a field he is selling, effective when he buys it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילא said: What about a person who tells his friend, 'This field I am selling you, once I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated'? Isn't it consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילא brings a comparison to show that a consecration can be set up now and take effect later. That is just what the woman is doing with her handiwork.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller says his consecration should only kick in once the field returns to him. If that works, then a woman can also consecrate handiwork that will only be hers after a divorce. The question 'isn't it consecrated?' means: obviously it is.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it become consecrated (הקדש).
When I buy it (back).
Is it not…? A way of saying 'of course it is.'
To his fellow, meaning another person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ila said:
And what if one says to his fellow,
"This field that I am selling to you,
when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated",
is it not consecrated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier ruling about a woman consecrating her handiwork.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman can consecrate handiwork that will only be hers in the future.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A field consecrated by its seller, effective when he buys it back.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the seller still owns the field now
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the comparison. The seller owns the field at the moment he speaks, but the woman does not control her handiwork now.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objected: Are these really alike? 'This field I am selling you': right now it is still in his hands. A woman, is it in her power to consecrate her handiwork?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on רבי אילא's comparison and points out a key difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller makes the consecration while he still owns the field, so he has the power to attach a condition. The woman's handiwork already belongs to her husband, so she has nothing in her hands to consecrate right now.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, meaning he challenges the statement.
Are they comparable?
In his hand, meaning he owns it or controls it.
Her handiwork, meaning what she earns from her work.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objects to it:
Are they comparable?
"This field that I am selling to you":
right now it is in his hand.
A woman, is it in her power to consecrate her handiwork?!
phrases.notes: Her handiwork goes to her husband during the marriage, so it isn't hers to give away.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי אילא's comparison, not the question itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The seller owns the field when he speaks; the woman does not control her handiwork when she speaks.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה's better comparison: a field already sold
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the true parallel is a field that was already sold, and there the consecration does not work. That points against the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like a person who tells his friend, 'This field I already sold you, once I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated.' Is it consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רבי אילא's case, רבי ירמיה offers the case he thinks really matches. That case suggests the woman's consecration fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the field is no longer his when he speaks, just as the handiwork is not the woman's. 'Is it consecrated?' means: of course not. So the woman's consecration should not work either.

keyTerms.meaning: This is only comparable to…
That I sold (already, in the past).
Is it consecrated? A way of saying 'of course not.'

phrases.english: This is comparable only
to one who says to his fellow,
"This field that I sold to you,
when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated",
is it consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמֵי אֶלָּא לָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison with one that cuts the other way.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a woman can consecrate her handiwork.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A field already sold cannot be consecrated by the former owner. The woman's handiwork is in the same position, so her consecration should not work.

steps.title: רב פפא: a sale is a clean break, marriage is not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects רבי ירמיה's comparison. A sale fully ends the seller's ownership, but the woman is not fully owned by her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: Are these alike?! With a sale, the matter is completely cut off. With a woman, is the matter completely cut off?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבי ירמיה's replacement case and shows it does not fit the woman either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a field is sold, the seller has no connection left to it. The husband only has rights to his wife's handiwork. She herself still belongs to herself, so her tie to her handiwork is not fully cut.

keyTerms.meaning: A sale.
The matter is cut off, meaning a complete and final break.
Regarding, in the case of.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it:
Are they comparable?!
Regarding a sale, their matter is cut off.
phrases.notes: Once a field is sold, the seller and the field are completely separated.

phrases.english: Regarding a woman, is the matter cut off?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's comparison from step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רבי ירמיה's comparison to a field already sold.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A sale is a total break from the field, but a wife keeps a connection to her handiwork.

steps.title: רב פפא's comparison: a pledged field
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the real parallel is a field the owner pledged, which he consecrates for when he redeems it. That does work, which supports the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like a person who tells his friend, 'This field I pledged to you, once I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated.' Isn't it consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers the case he thinks truly matches the woman. That case supports her consecration working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pledged field still belongs to the owner, but the lender has rights to it for now. That is just like the wife, who belongs to herself while her husband has rights to her handiwork. Since the pledged field becomes consecrated once redeemed, her consecration works once she is free.

keyTerms.meaning: That I pledged, meaning gave as security for a loan.
When I redeem it, meaning pay off the debt and get it back.

phrases.english: This is comparable only
to one who says to his fellow,
"This field that I pledged to you,
when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated",
is it not consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמֵי אֶלָּא לָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי ירמיה's case with one that supports the woman again.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's consecration of her handiwork takes effect later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A pledged field consecrated by its owner, effective when he redeems it.

steps.title: רב שישא: the owner can redeem anytime, the woman cannot divorce herself
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי rejects רב פפא's comparison. The owner can pay and redeem the field whenever he wants, but a woman cannot divorce whenever she wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי objected: Are these alike? With a field, it is in his power to redeem it. A woman, is it in her power to get divorced?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי finds a difference between the pledged field and the woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The field's owner controls when his field comes back, since he can just pay the debt. The woman cannot end her marriage on her own, so her case is weaker than an ordinary pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: To redeem it.
To become divorced.
The son of.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha son of Rav Idi objects to it:
Are they comparable?
A field: it is in his power to redeem it.
phrases.notes: He can pay back the loan anytime and take the field back.

phrases.english: A woman: is it in her power to be divorced?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's comparison from step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב פפא's comparison to an ordinary pledged field.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The field owner controls when he gets his field back; the woman does not control when her marriage ends.

steps.title: רב שישא's comparison: a field pledged for ten years
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא says the real parallel is a field pledged for a fixed ten years, which the owner cannot redeem early. Even so, the consecration works once he redeems it, which supports the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is only like a person who tells his friend, 'This field I pledged to you for ten years, once I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated.' Isn't it consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא gives the case that he says truly matches the woman, and it supports her consecration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a ten-year pledge, the owner cannot get his field back early. That matches the woman, who cannot end her marriage herself. The consecration still takes effect once the field is redeemed, so hers takes effect once she is free.

keyTerms.meaning: For ten years, meaning a fixed period during which the field cannot be redeemed.
Is comparable (another form of דָּמֵי).

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא here says 'מי דמי', meaning the comparison doesn't fit, and then offers a closer one. The last two cases, a pledged field and a field pledged for ten years, both support the idea that a woman's consecration of her handiwork can take effect later.
steps.confusionAlert: Watch the endings. 'מי קדשה?' (step 3) means 'it is NOT consecrated' and goes against the woman. 'מי לא קדשה?' (steps 5 and 7) means 'it IS consecrated' and supports her.

phrases.english: This is comparable only
to one who says to his fellow,
"This field that I pledged to you for ten years,
phrases.notes: For those ten years he can't pay early and take it back, just like the woman can't leave the marriage on her own.

phrases.english: when I redeem it from you, let it be consecrated",
is it not consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fixes רב פפא's comparison so it matches the woman's lack of control, and keeps the conclusion in her favor.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's consecration of her handiwork takes effect later.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A field pledged for ten years, consecrated effective when it is redeemed.

steps.title: רב אשי Rejects the Ten-Year Field Comparison
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ten-year pledged field is not like the woman. The field has a known end date, but a woman has no known end date for her husband's control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Are these cases really the same?! There, with the field, there is a fixed end date. Does a woman have a fixed end date?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי knocks down רב שישא's comparison from Step 7. He says the ten-year field and the woman are not really alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ten-year field, the owner knows exactly when the field will come back to him, so his consecration is aimed at a sure, set time. A woman has no set date when she will leave her husband's control, because she may never be divorced at all. That missing fixed end date is enough to break the comparison, so Step 7 no longer supports the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a later sage pushes back on what was just said)
Are they really alike? (the opening of a rejected comparison)
Fixed, set (has a known end date)
A fixed limit or set end date

steps.confusionAlert: רב שישא already showed the woman is like a field the owner cannot redeem early. רב אשי is raising a different point: it is not about whether she can end it early, but that nobody knows if or when it will end at all.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objects to it:
phrases.notes: He is pushing back on רב שישא's ten-year field comparison from the step before.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
There, it is fixed.
phrases.notes: "There" means the field pledged for ten years, where everyone knows the exact end date.

phrases.english: Does a woman have a fixed limit?
phrases.notes: Nobody knows if or when she will be divorced, so there is no set end date.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison offered by רב שישא in Step 7, just as Steps 4 and 6 rejected earlier comparisons.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the ten-year pledged field as a parallel to the woman. It does not decide the woman's case either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ten-year field has a fixed, known end date, while a woman's time under her husband's control has no set end and may never end.
steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא here says 'מי דמי', meaning the comparison doesn't fit, and most then offer a closer one. רבי אילא's sold field and רב פפא's pledged field supported the woman, and רבי ירמיה's already-sold field went against her. רב שישא's ten-year pledge supported her too, but רב אשי rejects even that, because a woman has no fixed end date. So by the end of the amud, no field comparison stands as proof either way.
